terms.comment: An imitation of the cat’s cry. We have found no Latin word for it in the reference works, and no vowel quantities are assigned to the sound.
Our working verb, made from the sound. Traupman and Andresian give fēliō, but that is the panther’s cry (below); we have found no other verb for a cat’s cry.
Andresian gives it for the cat’s cry, but in its one source, the late Carmen de philomela, it is the cry of the male panther (Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: clamo
Lewis & Short: felio
The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 287.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
